items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to enacting the "police reform
and reinvention act of 2022"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9114

SPONSOR: REICHLIN-MELNICK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to enacting the "police
reform and reinvention act of 2022"

 
PURPOSE:

To provide an ongoing framework for police departments to engage with
local communities to ensure that community stakeholders' inputs are
incorporated into the planning process and help make sure all New York-
ers feel safe, protected, and heard.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends the executive law by adding section 846-hh which
directs local governments with operating police agencies that previously
submitted their certification required by Executive Order 203 (EO 203)
issued on June 12, 2020, titled "New York State Police Reform and Rein-
vention Collaborative" to the director of the division of budget, to
provide a progress report every two years. The biennial progress report
will include steps taken by government entities and police agencies to
advance the goals and initiatives outlined in the improvement plan
developed in accordance with EO 203.

The biennial progress report will include the actions taken by the
government entity and the corresponding police agency to advance their
plan.The report will also include actions taken to address evidence-
based policing strategies.The chief executive of each local government
shall convene the head of the local police agency, community stakehold-
ers, the local office of the district attorney, and the local public
defender for no less than three public meetings to take feedback while
preparing the biennial progress report. The draft will be available for
public comment and then be presented to the local legislative body,
which shall ratify or adopt the plan no later than April 1, 2023; and
each odd-numbered year thereafter on April 1 of those years.

The local government will then certify to the director of the division
of budget that the police agency's plan has been adopted by the local
legislative body. Failure to submit the certification would result in
the division of budget being authorized, but not required, to withhold
state and federal funding for the local police agency until the certif-
ication is received and required to restore all such funding once the
certification is received. The Division of Criminal Justice Services
will have a copy of the biennial progress report available to the public
via the internet within thirty days of the local government adopting the
biennial progress report. By April 1, 2024 compliance with this section
of executive law will be a prerequisite for local policing agencies to
be accredited under the New York State Law Enforcement Accreditation
Program.

Section two provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In the midst of the national reckoning that followed the murder of
George Floyd by a Minneapolis police officer in May 2020, former Gover-
nor Andrew Cuomo issued Executive Order 203, which started a process to
create positive changes by bringing together police departments and
community members to propose reforms to community/police interactions
and policies. Across the state, the plans created by this process
contained meaningful steps toward bridging community divides and promot-
ing greater police/community goodwill. However, since the conclusion of
the EO 203 process on April 1, 2021, when plans were required to be
submitted to NYS, there has been no standardized way for members of the
public to evaluate whether departments have been making progress on the
recommendations and goals set forth in these plans.

This bill remedies that defect by setting up an ongoing process for
police departments and community members to come together every two
years to evaluate the progress towards reform and report to New York on
the progress toward the goals contained within the originally adopted
plans. Setting up this new biennial requirement will increase engagement
between police agencies and community stakeholders, will ensure that
community stakeholders' inputs are incorporated in the planning process,
create an environment of mutual partnership and trust, and will help
make sure all New Yorkers feel safe, protected, and heard.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Enacts the New York state police reform and reinvention collaborative to require any local government entity which has a police agency and which has previously transmitted to the director of the division of the budget the certification required by executive order number two hundred three issued on June twelfth, two thousand twenty to improve the police agency's deployments, strategies, policies, procedures, and practices, for the purposes of addressing the particular needs of the communities served by such police agency and promote community engagement to foster trust, fairness, and legitimacy, and to address any racial bias and disproportionate policing of communities of color; requires a biennial progress report; makes related provisions.
title: Enacts the "police reform and reinvention act of 2022"
